lgd_definition: “Livestock Guardian Dogs” means a dog that is specifically trained to work and/or live with domestic farm animals (i.e. cattle, sheep) without causing harm while aggressively repelling predators and is used exclusively for that purpose; “Farm Working Dog” means a dog that is specifically trained to and actively assists its owner(s) with herding and/or protection of livestock and where the owner(s) can demonstrative they are active livestock producers/farmers;
collar_tag_req: An Owner shall keep the Dog Tag securely affixed to the Dog’s collar or other restraining device whenever the Dog is off the owner’s property.
dog_limit: 3 Dogs in any Urban area of the Town. 5 Dogs in any Rural area of the Town.
notes: Very farm-friendly bylaw. Specifically defines both 'Farm Working Dog' and 'Livestock Guardian Dogs'. Allows up to 5 dogs in rural areas without a special exemption. The Town’s Fees and Charges By-law explicitly exempts 'livestock guardian dogs' and 'working dogs' from annual dog tag fees (No Charge).

collar_tag_req: The Town shall supply the owner with a dog tag and the owner shall always keep the tag securely affixed on the dog when the dog is off the property of the owner. No person shall remove the tag from a licensed dog, except while the dog is being lawfully used for hunting.
dog_limit: 3 dogs per household (Keeping 4 to 25 dogs requires a Kennel license, which mandates a 10-acre minimum lot size).
notes: Standard animal control bylaw. While the tag can be removed when a dog is lawfully used for hunting, there are no specific definitions, exemptions, or tag removal privileges mentioned for livestock guardian or herding dogs.

collar_tag_req: Every Owner of every dog shall renew his or her dog license once every calendar year. This section does not apply to a microchipped dog that has obtained a microchip dog tag.
dog_limit: 3 dogs per premises (more than 3 dogs requires a kennel license as defined in the Business Licensing By-law).
notes: Standard animal control bylaw. The bylaw’s title indicates it regulates animals ‘OTHER THAN FARM ANIMALS’, but it does not classify working dogs or LGDs as farm animals. No farm-friendly dog provisions found. Barking is handled under a separate Noise By-law.

collar_tag_req: All dogs must be licensed and bear a tag. Alternative identification (like tattoos/microchips) can be provided on the application.
dog_limit: No person shall keep more than three dogs in Dwelling - Single unit within the Township on all zoned properties.
notes: Standard animal care and control by-law. No LGD or working dog exemptions were found.

lgd_definition: “Working Dog” shall mean a dog trained, kept and utilized for work purposes including, but not limited to, livestock handling and/or guarding, pest and predator control, recreation dog sled use and police or rescue dogs;
collar_tag_req: Every owner shall affix to his dog a current license tag issued by the Municipality... and shall keep such tag affixed on the dog at all times when the dog is not on the owner’s property.
dog_limit: No owner shall have more than three (3) dogs in any dwelling unit. Keeping more than 3 dogs requires a Kennel license.
notes: Favourable to farm dogs. Defines ‘Working Dog’ to explicitly include livestock handling, guarding, and predator control. A ‘Personal Use Kennel’ license can be obtained to keep more than 3 dogs for specific purposes, explicitly including ‘predator control’.

collar_tag_req: Requires a system of licences under section 11(3).
dog_limit: 3 dogs (4 or more dogs constitutes a Kennel).
notes: A comprehensive animal care and control by-law with detailed standards for tethering and sheltering. Explicitly restricts excessive barking for more than 30 mins during the day or 20 mins at night. Does not include provisions or exemptions for working dogs or LGDs.

collar_tag_req: Guard dogs are required to be licenced and wear a tag.
dog_limit: A maximum of 3 dogs are permitted on any property not licenced as a kennel.
notes: URL NOT ACCESSIBLE. CivicWeb portal blocked web crawlers. Based on municipal meeting highlights from 2024, Mono recently reviewed its dog bylaw regarding Livestock Guardian Dogs, and the Town’s dog licensing portal provides a fee exemption ($0.00) for ‘Guard Dogs’, but the exact text and definitions from the bylaw could not be verified.

collar_tag_req: Requires registration and an identification tag.
dog_limit: 3 dogs per household (keeping 4 to 10 dogs constitutes a Hobby Kennel or Commercial/Breeding Kennel).
notes: Standard animal care and control bylaw. No agricultural or working dog definitions found, other than ‘Service Dog’.

lgd_definition: “Working Dog” means a dog that is trained specifically to assist police and other law enforcement personnel in their work.
collar_tag_req: Every owner of a dog shall keep an identification tag, securely affixed on the collar or harness on the dog at all times or have the dog microchipped. The tag may be removed while a dog is being lawfully used for hunting, herding or other similar activity.
dog_limit: 4 dogs in the Rural Area, 3 dogs in the Urban Area.
notes: The municipality no longer requires municipal dog tags or license fees for individual dogs, requiring only personal identification tags or microchips. Tags may be removed while dogs are actively herding or hunting. A higher limit of 4 dogs applies in rural areas compared to 3 in urban areas. The definition of ‘Working Dog’ is strictly limited to law enforcement dogs, but the herding tag exemption is farm friendly.

collar_tag_req: Every dog licensed under this by-law shall have their Oakville identification tag securely attached to the dog at all times.
dog_limit: Maximum of 3 dogs per premises, or any combination of six (6) dogs and cats maximum.
notes: Urban animal control by-law with comprehensive regulations on standards of care and an administrative penalty system. No farm dog or livestock guardian dog definitions/exemptions. Barking/noise is regulated under a separate Noise By-law.
